summary.headline: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA of INR56 crores, of which INR50 crores business EBITDA, with management reiterating FY27 annualised EBITDA of INR300-350 crores.
summary.overview: SG Mart delivered its strongest quarter by revenue (above INR1,800 crores) and EBITDA of INR56 crores in Q4 FY26, despite a disrupted March from the Middle East crisis. Underlying business EBITDA was about INR50 crores, with INR6 crores of inventory gain; FY26 EBITDA rose 35% to INR137 crores. Working capital was cut to 20 days, operating cash flow was about INR300 crores, and net cash closed at INR750 crores. Steel shortages hit the B2B trading volume and renewable structures, while service centres and the new steel profile business ramped up. Management kept FY27 guidance of INR300-350 crores annualised EBITDA, subject to war-related disruption.

segments.name: B2B metal trading
segments.commentary: Volume fell versus Q3 on steel supply shortage that began in January and worsened with the war; April and May commitments described as slow. EBITDA of INR700-1,000 per ton, and management says it contributes little to earnings.

segments.name: Service centres (India and Dubai)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume about 190,000-191,000 tons vs 163,000 tons in Q3, with Dubai at 37,000 tons (about 10%). Per-ton EBITDA of INR1,700-2,000. Stock-and-sell is about 20-25% of volume; cut-to-length about 75%.

segments.name: Renewable structures
segments.commentary: Q4 volume slightly down on coated steel shortage; monthly average about 5,000 tons. Per-ton EBITDA of INR3,000-5,000. FY27 volume guided at 130,000-150,000 tons; capacity is about 150,000 tons a year with no further capex needed.

segments.name: Steel profiles (incl. puff panels)
segments.commentary: New line launched in Q4 with about 7,000 tons, sold under APL Apollo brand and group network. April run-rate 5,000-6,000 tons. Per-ton EBITDA of INR5,000-8,000; puff panel margins guided at 5-8%. Profile capacity about 120,000 tons per annum; FY27 volume guided at 100,000+ tons.

guidance_outlook: FY27 annualised EBITDA guidance of INR300-350 crores retained; management said it should be near that unless war-related losses in B2B or Middle East operations deepen.
Quarterly business EBITDA of about INR50 crores expected to keep rising through FY27; management sees no deterioration in per-ton EBITDA spreads in Q1 FY27.
Renewable structures FY27 volume of 130,000-150,000 tons, with monthly volume rising from 5,000-6,000 to 8,000-9,000 tons once coated steel supply improves.
Service centre network to reach 11-12 by end of FY27 (three additions); FY27 renewable plus profile volumes expected above 230,000 tons combined.

Three-year targets: about 20 service centres at 8,000-10,000 tons per month each (about 2 million tons annualised exit run-rate), 250,000-300,000 tons renewables, 300,000 tons profiles; B2B volume not guided.
capex_capacity: Approved capex of about INR600 crores over FY27-FY28 described as the minimum; roughly one-third for service centre build-out, about half for land acquisition (at least four or five land parcels), and 15-20% for profile machines.
Land acquired in Ahmedabad, Indore and Kolkata; active scouting in Hyderabad, Chennai and Punjab, with more land acquisitions expected in the next two to three months.
Plan to add three service centres in FY27; a cut-to-length machine is being added at the Dubai centre.

Renewable capacity of about 150,000 tons is sufficient for FY27 with no new capex; additional lead time for machines is three to four months, and capacity is added once volume reaches about 10,000 tons per month for four to five months.
Puff panel capacity of 80,000 tons being set up against an industry size of about 150,000 tons (per the presentation).
demand_pricing: Steel supply shortage (linked to gas supply to steel mills) constrained B2B and coated steel supply; management expects improvement in May and June but says timing is unpredictable.
Dubai service centre (about 10% of volume) disrupted by the war; March business was almost nil and teams are only now returning.
Management says the company has moved away from low-margin B2B trading toward value-added verticals; trading is not expected to grow much.
Management says JSW and other platforms are in different product areas, with no direct overlap in SG Mart's value-added products.
Management stated the inventory loss in Q3 was about INR15-20 crores and the FY26 full-year EBITDA would have been above INR150 crores after adjusting for steel price swings.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost and other income decline QoQ despite a rise in cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed lower interest cost to working capital cut to 20 days and surplus cash. Net cash was INR750 crores vs INR740 crores in Q3, so the increase was only INR10 crores because of INR250 crores of capex.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27-28 capex plan and its split?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR600 crores approved over two years as the minimum, roughly one-third for service centres, half for land, and 15-20% for profile machines.

qa_highlights.question: What exercise price applies to the ESOP approval?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the exercise price is INR367, set about 1.5 years ago, and the approval covers balance unused ESOPs from the existing pool with no new issuance.

qa_highlights.question: Why does PAT growth lag EBITDA growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher depreciation from the fixed-asset build-out of service centres and renewable and profile capacity, plus interest cost. Management says cash profit growth should track EBITDA growth.

qa_highlights.question: What was the inventory impact on FY26 EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 had an inventory loss of about INR15-20 crores and Q4 an inventory gain of INR6 crores; H1 saw few price swings.

qa_highlights.question: What is per-ton EBITDA by vertical?
qa_highlights.answer: B2B INR700-1,000; B2B stable band INR1,800-2,100 (as stated); renewable structures INR3,000-5,000; steel profiles INR5,000-8,000; service centres INR1,700-2,000 per ton.

risks_watch: Steel and coated steel supply shortage linked to gas supply to mills; management says recovery depends on fuel supply and the war duration.
Dubai operations (about 10% of service centre volume) and Middle East disruption; management did not quantify the Dubai profit hit beyond fixed costs in March.
Unresolved analyst query on consolidated-minus-standalone gross margin and net block (about INR108 crores difference cited); management disputed the figure on the call and said it would revert.
Depreciation and interest costs are holding PAT growth (about 10-11%) well below EBITDA growth (35%); the gap is expected to persist for about two years of heavy capex.
Capital allocation: management plans no dividend for about two years; cash on books may be used for working capital as the business scales.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the value-added verticals and the medium-term EBITDA trajectory, but cautious and non-committal on near-term B2B volumes and monthly or quarterly guidance because of steel supply and the war. Several answers were deferred or left unclear, notably the Dubai net block and gross margin query and the ESOP price.
key_quotes: So the total reported EBITDA was INR56 crores, out of which business EBITDA was INR 50 crores and INR6 crores is the inventory gain.
We are confident that INR50 crores quarter 4 EBITDA, I mean, it will keep on rising throughout FY27, despite the challenges which we are facing in our B2B business due to the short supply of steel.
So we are not too much worried about that my PAT growth is not matching my EBITDA growth. It will start happening in a month in a year or so.
I think, it wouldn't be back -ended. You will see performance getting better and better every quarter, okay, from here on.
